title: Girona, In Reverse
title_candidates: One Hundred and Six, and Still Leading
theme: TEG 18 turned TEG 17 inside out: the man with three Wooden Spoons (Alex Baker) led the Trophy from R1 H5 to the last putt, the reigning Spoon holder (Gregg Williams) won the Green Jacket by 14, and the defending Trophy champion (Jon Baker) took the Spoon — a wire-to-wire procession won by the messiest card in the field.
tone: house — faithful, witty, tongue-in-cheek; Barney Ronay by way of Tom Peck, ribbing anchored in the numbers
opening_hook: Open on the final tableau at the Stadium course — Williams in the Jacket at +66, Alex Baker holding the Trophy on 169 with a 10 at the 14th still fresh on his card, Jon Baker holding the Spoon a year after holding the Trophy — then walk backwards through R4, R3, R2 to R1, where the whole thing was already decided at the 5th hole of the tournament: the further back you go, the more inevitable it looks.
foreshadow: Alex Baker arrived with three prior Wooden Spoons and the Spoon in two of the last three TEGs — the least likely wire-to-wire leader in the room
Gregg Williams arrived as reigning Wooden Spoon holder (TEG 17) and opened with a 27-over-par R1
Jon Baker arrived as defending Trophy champion (TEG 17) and led the Green Jacket race after both Tour rounds
The 'more forgiving' Tour course was quietly waiting to produce the worst gross round in its 22-visit TEG history

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Alex Baker (winner, 169 pts, by 8 from John Patterson)
competitions.how: Alex Baker took the outright lead at R1 H5 after two routine early exchanges and was never headed across the remaining 67 holes: 46 in R1, 41 in R2, 44 in R3, 38 in R4, with the lead 12/11/12/8 at the four checkpoints. The remarkable part is the method — he built it on hot stretches (b07, b14, b04) while simultaneously posting an 11, a 10, a 9 and two 8s, and the Tour course-worst 106 (cr02). Patterson closed to 8 but never got a look at the front.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams (winner, +66, by 14 from David Mullin)
competitions.how: Jon Baker led the gross race after both Tour rounds, holding the outright lead for 20 holes from R1 H5 until a bogey at R2 H7 handed it to Williams (b03). Williams took it outright for good with a par at R3 H2 (b09) and then simply pulled away on the Stadium: rounds of 27, 14, 13, 12 over par, a lead of 8 after R3 and 14 after R4, sealed with a new personal best 84 at the Stadium in R4. Mullin's course-record 84 in R3 (cr01) was brilliant and 14 shots too late.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: The defending Trophy champion was bottom after R1, escaped to 4th with a 39-point R2, then dropped to the bottom again at R3 H2 (b31) and stayed there for the rest of the tournament — a quintuple bogey 9 at R3 H4 (b17) and five straight doubles in R4 (b46) made sure of it. Rounds of 30, 39, 28, 29; 8 shots worse at the Stadium than his last visit. Mullin's R1 11 at the 15th (b10, b61) had put him briefly at the bottom, but the Spoon changed hands for the last time on the second green of R3.

headline_candidates: Forty-Six Points and a Nine: the Baker Method
Alex Baker Takes Something He Usually Hands Over
Mullin's 11 at the 15th and the Tour Course's Opening Statement
rounds.chosen_headline: Forty-Six Points and a Nine: the Baker Method
rounds.angle: Alex Baker posts 46 points with a quad at the 2nd and a 9 at the last, takes the outright lead at H5 and is never seen again from behind; Patterson bleeds 22 shots in eight holes, Mullin's 11 at the 15th drops him to the bottom, and Williams — last year's Spoon holder — signs for 27 over.

headline_candidates: One Hundred and Six, and Still Leading
An 11 at the Last, and the Trophy Lead Intact
Jon Baker's Twenty Holes in Front End at the 7th
rounds.chosen_headline: One Hundred and Six, and Still Leading
rounds.angle: Alex Baker writes himself into the Tour course's record book for the wrong reason — 106 gross, the worst in 22 TEG visits, with an 8 at the 16th and an 11 at the 18th — and still leads the Trophy by 11; meanwhile Jon Baker's 20-hole grip on the Jacket race quietly ends with a bogey at the 7th.

headline_candidates: Spain's Premier Course Finally Gives Up a Number
rounds.angle: On the second hole of R3 the tournament resolves itself twice — Williams takes the Jacket lead for good, Jon Baker drops to the bottom for good — while Mullin shoots 84 to break a Stadium record that had stood through 27 prior visits, and Alex Baker answers a five-hole bleed with 21 points from the 11th to the 16th.

headline_candidates: Williams Takes the Jacket by 14; Baker Wins Despite Himself
A Ten at the 14th, an Eight at the 17th, a Trophy at the 18th
From Spoon to Jacket in One Year
rounds.chosen_headline: Williams Takes the Jacket by 14; Baker Wins Despite Himself
rounds.angle: Williams closes with his own 84 at the Stadium to win the Jacket at +66 by 14; Alex Baker signs off with a 10 at the 14th and an 8 at the 17th and still wins the Trophy by 8; Jon Baker's five consecutive doubles confirm the Spoon.

players.arc: Three prior Wooden Spoons and the Spoon in two of the last three TEGs, and yet he led from the 5th hole of R1 to the final green — 169 points, seventh best in TEG history, assembled around an 11, a 10, a 9, two 8s and the worst gross round the Tour course has ever seen.
Arrived as the reigning Wooden Spoon holder, opened 27 over par, then went 14-13-12 over on the way to the Green Jacket at +66 by 14, finishing with a personal-best 84 at the Stadium.
Defending Trophy champion who led the gross race for 20 holes and after two rounds, then lost the Jacket at R2 H7, the plot at R3 H2 and the Spoon race to nobody at all — 126 points and the Spoon.
Nine prior Jacket wins and one very odd tournament: 10 shots worse than his last Tour visit with an 11 at the 15th, then the new Stadium course record of 84 in R3 — Jacket runner-up by 14.
Bled 22 shots in eight holes on the first morning, then quietly assembled personal bests on both Catalunya courses and the Trophy runner-up spot, 8 points adrift.

cuts: b09 (keep as a line in R3, not a section)
venue_notes: TEG's 4th visit to Catalonia, and a familiar pair of tracks: the Tour course for R1 and R2 (its 5th and 6th TEG rounds), the Stadium for R3 and R4 (its 6th and 7th). Lean on the irony that the Tour — billed as the more forgiving sibling — produced the worst gross round in 22 TEG visits (cr02) and Mullin's 11 at the 15th, while Spain's premier championship course, the Stadium, gave up its lowest TEG score ever twice in two days (Mullin's record 84 in R3, matched by Williams's 84 in R4).
course_history_notes: Mullin's new personal best at the Stadium in R3 — 84 gross, 7 better than his previous best there (TEG 11) and 8 better than his last visit — the same week he was 10 shots worse than his last visit to the Tour course.
Williams matched the number a day later: a new personal best 84 at the Stadium in R4, 8 better than both his prior best there (TEG 12) and his last visit.
Patterson set new personal bests on both courses — 94 at the Tour in R2 and 93 at the Stadium in R3, each 2 better than his TEG 12 marks.
Jon Baker was 8 shots worse than his last visit to the Stadium; Alex Baker was 7 worse there, and still won the Trophy.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R1 H5 on the Tour course — Alex Baker retakes the outright lead after the only three lead changes of the week and holds it for the next 67 holes, the margin never dropping below 8.
Green Jacket: R3 H2 at the Stadium (b09) — Williams's par takes the outright gross lead from Jon Baker for good, and turns into an 8-shot cushion by nightfall and 14 by the finish.
Wooden Spoon: R3 H2 at the Stadium (b31) — Jon Baker's triple bogey drops him to the bottom, and the quintuple 9 at the 4th (b17) two holes later ends any argument.

payoffs.seed: Alex Baker's three prior Spoons / Spoon in two of the last three
payoffs.payoff: He takes the lead at R1 H5 and never loses it — 169 points (b02), the 7th-highest Trophy total in TEG history, from the man who had been picking up the Spoon.

payoffs.seed: Gregg Williams as reigning Wooden Spoon holder, 27 over in R1
payoffs.payoff: Jacket lead taken at R3 H2 (b09), then +66 and a 14-shot win (b01) with a personal-best 84 at the Stadium in R4 — Spoon to Jacket in twelve months.

payoffs.seed: Jon Baker, defending champion, leading the gross race after both Tour rounds
payoffs.payoff: The 20-hole gross lead ends with a bogey at R2 H7 (b03); he drops to the bottom of the Spoon race at R3 H2 (b31) and finishes with it on 126 (b13).

payoffs.seed: The 'more forgiving' Tour course waiting to produce something historic
payoffs.payoff: Alex Baker's 106 (cr02) — the worst gross round in 22 TEG visits to the Tour — complete with the 8 at the 16th and the 11 at the 18th (b05), posted by the tournament leader.
